To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pyramidal tracts of mammals are composed of synchronously conducting bundles that arise from clusters of neurons in cortical gray matter.

(1) neighboring pyramidal neurons in the cerebral cortex are interconnected by a dense network of collaterals, (2) this interconnection is reciprocal, (3) these neurons are organized in groups of 2-4 cells that share common collaterals and project to the same target structures, (4) these groups of neurons project synchronously, and (5) these synchronous projections are mediated by synchronously conducting fiber bundles.

pyramidal tract fibers from neighboring neurons in the cerebral cortex assemble to form a bundle that conducts synchronously, and that this bundle of fibers is a functional unit that transmits information from cerebral cortex to the spinal cord.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization and function of the pyramidal tracts, which are the main output system of cerebral cortex and the major source of cortically generated motor activity.
the functional anatomy of the pyramidal system.
the anatomical and physiological organization of the cerebral cortex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fibers from a cluster of pyramidal tract cells conduct synchronously in the pyramidal pathway.
the superimposition of antidromically evoked spikes is not due to collision of action potentials in a single neuron, but rather to synchronous activation of neighboring neurons in clusters.
the pyramidal fibers from a small cluster of neurons in the cerebral cortex assemble to form a bundle of fibers that conduct synchronously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pyramidal tract fibers from small clusters within cerebral cortex conduct synchronously.
pyramidal tract axons are not independent of one another, but are organized into clusters, and these clusters project to different targets.
the pyramidal system is not a homogeneous collection of neurons, but rather is a heterogeneous population of neurons that are organized in small groups of neurons that conduct synchronously.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pyramidal tracts contain synchronously conducting fibers.
, in the pyramidal system, the fibers of individual cells are not independent of one another but rather are assembled into bundles that conduct synchronously.

neurons in the cerebral cortex are organized into small, tightly interconnected clusters of cells, each of which is represented in the corticospinal tract as an individual bundle of fibers that projects to a different spinal cord target.
